sources.note: Nothing: 0 hits for 'stress' or 'accent' in the whole article. Pero is treated as tonal: a 'tone change linked with the vowel assimilation' where 'the tone of the perfective suffix na has been shifted onto the verb root' (p. 63), and Rule 26 VOWEL DELETION II deletes a morpheme-final low-toned vowel 'along with its tone' (p. 69). No tone inventory or stress statement; the article covers vowels only and refers consonants to Frajzyngier 1978.

sources.note: Classes Pero as a two-tone (2T) language in its appendix table of tone inventories and question markers, and lists Pero (after Frajzyngier 1989) among the languages with rising question intonation / final H (p. 44), with an [open]-vowel question marker (p. 45) and with the low-tone-or-falling / lengthening question marker spread across the Sudanic belt (p. 50). No analysis of Pero lexical tone beyond the '2T' label.

sources.citation: Kraft, Charles H. 1981. Chadic Wordlists, Volume I (Plateau-Sahel). (Marburger Studien zur Afrika- und Asienkunde, Serie A: Afrika, 23.) Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. 265 pp. [Pero list pp. 99 ff; digitised as lexibank/kraftchadic (CLDF, CC-BY-4.0)]
sources.note: Data only: the digitised Pero list (406 forms) is tone-marked - 372 forms carry tone diacritics: 424 grave (low), 63 caron (rising), 19 circumflex (falling), 3 macron; unmarked vowels = high; also 11 tildes - i.e. a two-level (H/L) transcription with rising and falling contours on single vowels (e.g. 'jɔlâ cɔlɔ̀' pull, 'cinə̀' lie down, 'karà' cut); no prose statement of the tone system in the digitised rows (Kraft's printed introduction unseen).

tone.summary: Transcription implies 2 level tones (H unmarked, L grave) plus falling (circumflex) on some syllables; no analysis.
